grandparents_cupboard.reason: Oats, fresh fruit, raisins, nuts, seeds and cinnamon are all plain home-cupboard foods with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Every item, including the hazelnuts and pumpkin seeds, is an everyday line at any big supermarket.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a bowl, a grater and a knife and board, with hand squeezing and grating well within a beginner's reach.

works.reason: 200g oats soaked in two oranges' juice plus 400ml water, then loosened with grated apple, gives a sensible set texture and four 50g-oat portions.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes split across the evening and morning covers squeezing, grating two apples, halving 300g grapes and chopping nuts, and the 480 minutes is the unattended overnight soak.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the lemon and cinnamon, appears in the steps, and red grapes are simply grapes.

seasonal_feel.reason: A 300g heap of grapes with orange and apple makes the fruit the point, and a cold oat breakfast is ordinary in November.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear and in plain British English, such as 'loosen with a splash of water if thick'.

hearty_healthy.reason: Oats, three fruits, nuts and seeds make a filling breakfast with no added sugar.
